newsitem.title: USA: Island nations blast Clinton climate change plan.
newsitem.headline: Island nations blast Clinton climate change plan.

text.p: Representatives of island nations on Thursday blasted the Clinton administration for offering a weak plan to fight global climate change which they said could devastate their countries.
"Island nations around the world are in enormous danger of disappearing under the ocean," Lionel Hurst, ambassador from Antigua and Barbuda, said at a briefing.

Hurst said his country sent Vice President Al Gore a letter calling for a stronger U.S. plan to "start moving as quickly as possible" to reduce emissions from burning fossil fuels that trap heat in the atmosphere.
Islands are threatened by rising sea levels caused by warmer water temperatures and melting glaciers, and by more intense storms, brought on by global warming.

"Why is the United States' position so wishy-washy? I believe it is because they are only hearing the voices of the oil lobbyists, the fossil fuels lobbyists," Minister Counsellor Espen Ronneberg of the Marshall Islands Republic said at the briefing.

"The United States is taking a position that nothing can be done in the short-term. They are rejecting our short-term goals," said Ronneberg, who represents the Marshall Islands in the United Nations and is the delegate to the Alliance of Small Island States (AOSIS).
The Clinton administration's plan, submitted in international negotiations on binding measures to fight climate change, calls for emissions-cutting to start in 2010.

Most environmentalists say reductions must start by 2005 to avoid further serious global warming, and many criticised the Clinton administration's plan of international trading of emissions "permits" as too full of loopholes to succeed.
"From the Clinton administration, we get these very strong statements...then we get this position paper. There's no correlation," Ronneberg said.
